title: Self-Host: Large file resumable upload always uses port 8000
body: I am self-hosting Supabase with KONG_HTTP_PORT=8089 and the public URLs set to https://myhost:44307. Small Storage uploads correctly use the external HTTPS URL and port. Large files that require resumable uploads instead generate URLs such as http://myhost:8000/storage/v1//upload/resumable/..., ignoring the external port. I expect large-file resumable uploads to use https://myhost:44307/storage/v1/upload/resumable/... like small uploads do. My host OS is Windows, with supabase/studio:2025.11.10-sha-5291fe3, kong:2.8.1, and supabase/storage-api:v1.29.0.

symptoms_visible: Small Storage uploads use https://myhost:44307, but large resumable uploads generate an http://myhost:8000/storage/v1//upload/resumable/... URL.
N0.label: N0 incorrect resumable upload URL reported

symptoms_visible: I access both small and large uploads through https://myhost:44307, but only the large upload is redirected to http://myhost:8000.
N1.label: N1 proxy topology clarified

symptoms_visible: After applying the suggested reverse-proxy and Kong trusted-IP configuration, the large-file upload still uses the wrong URL.
N2_x.label: N2_x forwarded-header workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: Even when I bypass HTTPS and access http://IP:8089 directly, a large upload still sends the subsequent resumable request to port 8000.
N3.label: N3 Kong internal-port behavior confirmed

symptoms_visible: A maintainer reports that Storage now supports an explicit public URL for resumable uploads, but I have not retested that change on my own system.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix available but reporter not retested

question_patterns: How are ports 44307 and 8089 connected in your deployment?
Is there an additional reverse proxy in front of Kong, or are you bypassing Kong?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Port 44307 is my reverse-proxy port. It exposes my domain over HTTPS and forwards to Kong on port 8089.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no reverse proxy; Kong itself listens publicly on port 8000, which is also the URL I use in the browser.
The same reverse-proxy arrangement is used, but the external HTTPS port is 443 instead of 44307.

question_patterns: What browser URL do you use when starting small and large uploads?
Can you provide the initial and subsequent request URLs for a large upload?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I start both small and large uploads from https://myhost:44307. Small uploads keep using that address, while the large upload endpoint becomes http://myhost:8000/storage/api/upload.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The browser itself starts the large upload from an http://myhost:8000 page, so there is no change of protocol or port in the response.

edges.comment: Reporter c4 clarifies the original reporter's own topology: an HTTPS reverse proxy on 44307 forwards to Kong on 8089, while the large-upload URL alone changes to HTTP port 8000.

solution.intent: Keep the reverse proxy and Kong in the request path, make the proxy send the external forwarded protocol and port, and configure Kong to trust that proxy so it preserves those values for Storage.
solution.concrete_example: Configure the proxy to send X-Forwarded-Proto: https and X-Forwarded-Port: 44307, then add the proxy address to KONG_TRUSTED_IPS and retry after clearing browser local storage.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer inferred that Storage constructs the resumable Location URL from forwarded headers and that untrusted proxy headers are replaced with Kong's internal HTTP/8000 values. The reporter supplied the topology and observed URLs, not this causal interpretation.

edges.comment: Maintainers c9 and c18 proposed forwarded headers plus KONG_TRUSTED_IPS for the original reporter's reverse-proxy deployment. Reporter c19 replied that it did not work in their setup and attached the shown configuration, so this specific attempt is a known blind path for this case.

question_patterns: As a diagnostic test, what happens if you access Kong directly on port 8089 without the HTTPS proxy?
Please start a large upload through http://IP:8089 and report the initial request and the subsequent resumable URL.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Even when I access http://IP:8089 directly without HTTPS, the large upload still sends its subsequent request to http://IP:8000. I've attached the Network screenshot.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: When I access http://IP:8089 directly, all resumable requests remain on port 8089 and the upload succeeds.
The direct test still changes from port 8089 to 8000, but the generated path has only one slash.

edges.comment: Reporter c20 performs a temporary direct-access probe on their own deployment. The raw result is only that a request begun on HTTP port 8089 receives a resumable URL on port 8000; interpreting this as Kong exposing its internal listener is engineer-side.

solution.intent: Use a Storage build and Docker Compose configuration that supports an explicit STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL for TUS resumable URLs, set it to the externally reachable Supabase URL, and have the reporter verify the returned Location header and chunk requests before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Update to a Storage/Compose setup with STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL support and set STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL=https://myhost:44307 (the Compose default can derive it from SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL). Then upload a file larger than 6 MB and confirm that the POST Location header and later PATCH requests remain on https://myhost:44307.
solution.inference_hint: The direct 8089-to-8000 probe supports the maintainer's diagnosis that the resumable Location is derived from Kong's internal listener information rather than the public URL variables. The final thread update states that Storage gained STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL specifically to tell TUS which external URL to use; the original reporter never confirmed it on their installation.

edges.comment: Maintainer c35 records the final technical remedy: Storage gained STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL and Docker Compose wires it from SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL by default. This update came after closure, and the original reporter did not retest, so the terminal records fix availability rather than a user-confirmed resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: resumable uploads use a Location URL constructed by Storage from proxy information, and Kong can pass its internal HTTP port 8000 values instead of the externally reachable HTTPS host and port.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the observed split between small and resumable uploads, the reverse-proxy-to-Kong topology, and the direct http://IP:8089 probe that still produced a port-8000 resumable URL.

The durable final recommendation must use Storage's explicit public URL configuration for TUS, setting STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL to the externally reachable Supabase URL, rather than assuming SITE_URL or API_EXTERNAL_URL alone controls resumable Location headers.
Must not claim that the forwarded-header and KONG_TRUSTED_IPS attempt resolved this reporter's deployment; the reporter said that attempted configuration did not work.
Must ask the reporter to verify a file larger than 6 MB by checking the Location header and subsequent chunk requests on a build containing the public-URL support.
Must not declare the original reporter's system resolved, because the thread contains no reporter confirmation after the final Storage configuration support became available.

persona_hint.experience_level: Self-hosting operator comfortable editing environment variables, Docker configuration, and reverse-proxy ports, and able to inspect browser Network requests, but needs guidance for tracing forwarded headers through Kong and Storage.
persona_hint.communication_style: Brief and direct; supplies concrete ports, URLs, screenshots, and test results, and asks practical verification questions when configuration advice does not work.
